question: Let It Be and Zombie loop the same four chords. Why does one sound hopeful and the other bleak?
answer: Because each enters the loop at a different chord. Let It Be cycles C, G, A minor, F; Zombie cycles roughly E minor, C, G, D, the same circle entered at its minor chord. A loop has no fixed beginning, so the chord heard first becomes home. Same circle, different front door.
move: Where a cycle begins can decide what it seems to mean.
ask: Where I start the story of my life, does that decide whether it feels hopeful or bleak?

scene.hint: Switch on one loop, then swap it for the other. Same four chords, another start.

tracks.name: Hope
tracks.text: Let It Be: C, G, Am, F. The loop starts on C, so C feels like home.

tracks.name: Bleak
tracks.text: Zombie: Am, F, C, G. The same four chords, entered at A minor. It aches.

moments.text: Both at once clash on every beat: the order really is the whole difference.

reference: Everett, The Foundations of Rock: From Blue Suede Shoes to Suite: Judy Blue Eyes, Oxford University Press, 2009
